The proposal seeks operator control of TYPE, UNIT and HELP, including corrections, metadata-preserving renames and HELP removal.

The suggested A+B approach combines post-relabel authoritative type/unit with a family stage supplying HELP and initial metadata.
No final decision is recorded; API/cache semantics, per-series variants and dropped-family metadata remain unresolved.
Per-series type/unit overrides can disagree within one family, which the family-keyed scrape cache and metadata API cannot represent cleanly.
Relabeling incurs per-series cost and accepts typos such as guage without value validation.
HELP is large and non-identifying, and the existing relabel approach does not reach OTLP or RW receive.
A+B is suggested, but cache/API behavior and the final design are not decided.

A whole-series hash can keep series distinct after label_replace removes their distinguishing label, hiding the normal duplicate-labelset error.
Hashing only removed labels is suggested to preserve detection when the remaining distinguishing dimension is destroyed.

The supplied exchange does not establish a final upstream resolution.

Integer comparison avoids slower string comparison and wasteful binary-to-string encoding.
The author reports faster million-series Thanos deduplication by reusing the stored uint64 without encoding/decoding, with extra engine code required.
An explicit +Inf bound produces one +Inf sample in the bounds loop and another synthesized from Count.
Valid producer data yields equal values; divergent values require a count/bucket-sum violation.
#19425 skips the explicit +Inf bound and emits only the synthesized count bucket with a deduplicated warning.
Exemplars attached to the skipped bound still reach the synthesized bucket.
The NHCB path rejects explicit +Inf through checkHistogramCustomBounds, whereas #19425 normalizes it and warns.
Skipping the bound keeps the histogram flowing and avoids the duplicate write; -Inf remains unaffected.
Warning versus returning an error is left to maintainers; no final decision is supplied.
histogram_1 declares count=15 but bucket_counts={3,11,0} sum to 14, so the expected native histogram fails Validate.
The declared sum=155 requires an overflow observation, so #19429 sets the last bucket to 1.
Classic expectations stay unchanged; the native bucket delta changes from -11 to -10.
Expected native histograms in the affected TestFromMetrics block now undergo Validate before comparison.
The maintainer says the count=1/no-buckets fixtures do not seem deliberate and permits adding a minimal bucket.
Commit a89fd357b adds minimal buckets and Validate checks to the TestTemporality exponential-histogram fixtures.
#19911 proposes warning when scrape_interval + scrape_timeout >= lookback_delta.
A long scrape can let the previous up sample leave lookback before the failed scrape writes its sample, briefly removing up and resetting alert state.
The reviewer objects that scrape-start timestamps allow valid configurations and correction requires understanding alert rules.
The supplied discussion has no final decision on changing the lint.
#19427 adds experimental promtool tsdb check-histograms [--min-time=..] [--max-time=..] [db path].
It reports non-monotonic buckets, +Inf/count disagreement, invalid le values, conflicting duplicate le spellings and missing +Inf buckets.
Findings cause a non-zero exit; disjoint-time le="1" and le="1.0" migration series are treated as clean.
Native histograms are out of scope, and the selected range’s bucket series are held in memory.
query instant/range already supported --header, but series/labels did not forward custom headers such as X-Scope-OrgID.
#19335 adds --header to promtool query series and query labels and passes the header map through QuerySeries/QueryLabels.
The change includes request-header tests for both commands and regenerated CLI documentation.
Exemplars rely on WAL replay because blocks do not store them; compaction can drop their series identity while retaining exemplar records.
#19940 tracks the latest accepted exemplar timestamp and preserves series identity until it falls below the replay cutoff.
Protection covers ordinary, selected and stale compaction and is restored from WAL or memory snapshots.
Selected/stale compaction can still replay already-persisted samples; no durable per-series compaction boundary is added.
Snapshot recovery loses expiry timestamps for references outside Head, including aliases, so later checkpoints can retain samples without their series records.
#19590 persists bounded expiry records and restores them before WAL replay, advancing the series ID counter to avoid reuse.
Older snapshots fall back to full WAL replay with WAL enabled and remain readable with WAL disabled; agent mode is outside scope.
Targeted tests pass, but the broader race run did not pass and was not repeated.

Amazon MQ offers RabbitMQ and ActiveMQ; RabbitMQ’s Prometheus metrics support motivates this addition.

Exponentiation binds tighter than unary signs, so printing inf ^ 2 as +Inf ^ 2 changes the parsed AST and yields ++Inf ^ 2 on the next print.
#19821 makes String() and Pretty() parenthesize signed left operands, producing (+Inf) ^ 2.
For code-built ASTs, omitting parentheses around -2 changes the intended squared result from 4 to -4.

Live stored classic samples shadow converted NHCB samples for the entire histogram group at that timestamp.
Disjoint migration ranges merge into continuous series, preferring live samples at cutover and dropping delayed old-representation staleness.

Source-order-dependent hashing makes StartTimestamp return 0 instead of 3000 ms when calls_total and calls_created have reversed equivalent label orders.

Streaming NHCBParser expects one label set’s _bucket, _count and _sum series contiguously.
Ungrouped ordering emits incomplete bucket-only histograms with Sum=0, duplicate count-only histograms and drops trailing sums.
Such ordering is allowed by Prometheus text format but violates OpenMetrics interleaving rules.
